messages:
Asha Bhat: Heads up — security pinged me this morning about raw user identifiers in OpenTelemetry spans being exported to third-party exporters. They asked for a recommendation: redaction at the agent vs encryption at the exporter boundary. Thoughts? :eyes:

Mike L: Big tradeoff. Redaction is simple and removes risk but breaks debugging & attribution. Encryption keeps data usable but adds KMS/key-management and latency.

Samir Patel: Are we mainly worried about attributes like `user.email`, `user.id`, `org.id`, `session_id`? If so we can pseudonymize most fields (e.g. `user_email_hash`) and keep a separate encrypted blob for raw values.

Eva Chen: Perf note — doing per-attribute encryption in the hot path will increase CPU and might add 10-30% p95 tail depending on implementation. We should consider batching encryption or delegating to a sidecar.

Asha Bhat: Security also wants an audit trail: who decrypted/unmasked values and when. That pushes towards encryption + KMS + access-logging rather than irreversible redaction. :lock: :key:

telemetry-bot: New RFC draft created: https://go/internal/rfcs/telemetry-pii-handling — summary pinned in doc.

Samir Patel: Architecturally I like a policy-driven approach: annotate spans with `pii_level` and have processors enforce masking/encryption based on tenant/exporter policy. Exporters can optionally request a decryption token if they meet compliance.

Mike L: Example processor config for OTEL collector could look like this (rough):

```yaml
processors:
  pii_mask:
    rules:
      - key: user.email
        action: hash
      - key: user.id
        action: encrypt
    encryption:
      kms_key: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/telemetry/cryptoKeys/span
      mode: aes-gcm
```

Eva Chen: Two concerns: 1) encrypted attributes become opaque and you lose indexed searchability (we rely on `user_id` for many traces dashboards). 2) storage/retention of encrypted blobs and access paths is extra infra.

Asha Bhat: Hybrid proposal: store a hashed/pseudonymized ID in the span for indexing, and store the raw attributes encrypted in a secure blob store keyed by `span_id`. Access to the raw blob requires KMS unwrap + audit approval. That gives searchability without leaking raw PII.

Samir Patel: That seems workable. Implementation notes: ensure the mapping blob -> span_id is immutable, rotate keys monthly, and support emergency legal-hold read paths. Need to ensure blobs are also replicated securely for Dedicated/Private deployments.

SecBot: Security checklist for the RFC: KMS integration + key rotation policy, per-tenant key scoping, audit logging for decrypt operations, retention TTL enforcement, HSM support for Private, and legal/forensic access controls. I can sync with legal.

Mike L: I can run perf experiments measuring AES-GCM overhead and memory for storing blobs. Will prototype encrypting a small set of attributes in the collector and measure end-to-end p95. :thumbsup:

Asha Bhat: I'll open the RFC with threat model, proposed configs, and a canary plan for one exporter (start with our internal observability exporter, then Datadog). Assigning action items: Samir -> prototype collector processor; Mike -> perf numbers; Eva -> infra cost/ops impact; Sec -> finalize checklist.

telemetry-bot: asha created doc https://go/internal/rfcs/telemetry-pii-handling and added reviewers @security @observability. Next steps recorded.
